subtopic: Small Account Balances and Fee Erosion
source_evidence: for investment advisory accounts with lower balances, small monthly fees like these can add up to a large percentage of the amount invested, and can end up being more expensive than traditional asset-based fees.
answer: A subscription fee is a set recurring charge, so its impact depends partly on the size of your account. The same monthly fee takes up a larger share of a small balance than of a large one. For example, a $3 monthly fee totals $36 over a year. On a $500 account, that is 7.2% of the account’s value. Fees can also make it harder for a smaller account to grow: as fees reduce the balance, they become a larger percentage of the money remaining.
